title: Nicholas Wotton to Queen Mary, June 1554 (BL Harley MS 1582 ff. 8-10; DECODE R8499)

steps.what: Fetched R8499 record and 6 full-resolution images with the session cookie.
CSP Foreign Mary, June and July 1554 (BHO): only Wotton to Petre 14 June and to the Queen 14/29 July; this letter not calendared. Cryptiana has only Wotton's 1548 cipher.
Transcribed four cipher pages sign by sign in ad-hoc tokens (3,152 signs, 150 types) plus clear connectives; identified sender (Wotton) and recipient (the Queen) from the clear text.
Blind homophonic annealing (en-1640s): first solver collapsed (model artefact on 'eeee'); rewritten incremental annealer solved synthetic controls, but not R8499.
Synthetic English under 100/150-sign homophonic keys: 100% recovered clean; 1 run in 3 at 10% noise; fails at 20% noise.
DECODE R354 (SP 106/2 f. 162, France 1554): alphabet, nulls and nomenclator (Carew, the rebels, the Constable, Lady Elizabeth ...) of Wotton's 1554 cipher.

Nulls removed, key codes and letter values pinned, rest annealed: partial English (Compiegne, the rebels, the Constable, fair words, the pensions, the Low Countries, the resolution taken between the Constable and Carew).
Direct reading of p1.02 against the key: 'Compiegne and spake of ... with your highness the rebels with the Constable'.
Key-aligned readings of every line by 5 agents from the images, then 2 regrade passes with merged keys: p1-2 46.0% (744/1616), p3+p6 48.5% (644/1329) of signs read as sense.
Merged tokens re-checked on the images and split into precise labels (transcription_v2.txt); pinned anneal on v2 reads more sense, still well below 95%.
v3 regrade on the image-checked transcription: 2061/2737 non-null signs read (75.3%, incl. tentative); firm about 60%.
v4: unified key; 1765/2736 non-null signs read firmly (64.5%), 79.5% incl. tentative.
Full-resolution sign-by-sign passes on pages 1-2: p1 66% firm, p2 74% firm; whole letter 2016/2749 firm (73.3%).
Full-resolution sign-by-sign passes on pages 3 and 6; whole letter 1971/2750 firm (71.7%), 88.3% incl. tentative.
Unified key v6 and full transcription of the R354 nomenclator (~140 entries); whole letter 2092/2797 firm (74.8%), 89.2% incl. tentative.
Full nomenclator tested against every unread stretch: few codes fit; whole letter 75.0% firm, 89.5% incl. tentative (v7).

Full-resolution shape pass: ^ and C each split into two shapes matching their context values; rare codes absent from R354; name lookup proposes 'Brymstane, a Scot'. 75.0% firm, 89.4% incl. tentative (v8).

Harleian catalogue 1808 and BL catalogue: ff. 5r-7v is a contemporary copy deciphering ff. 8-10 (13 June 1554, Soissons); not digitised and not on DECODE. Tytler ii, CSP Scotland i and DECODE key search found nothing further.

gaps.item: ~25% of non-null signs (names, Ie, rare codes, p1 runs)
gaps.detail: contemporary decipherment ff. 5r-7v not digitised; order BL images
no entry on the only surviving key copy R354

outcome.notes: Read in part with key R354 after eight transcription/key passes: 75.0% of 2,801 non-null signs firm, 89.4% incl. tentative (final_v8.txt). The contemporary decipherment (Harley 1582 ff. 5r-7v) is not digitised; ~40 rare codes are not on R354.

prior.where: Harley MS 1582 ff. 5r-7v, contemporary deciphered copy (not digitised)

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up the coding agent with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
